_about: Minimized mismatches between runtime/scripts/deny-hook.sh and real bash, found by scripts/deny_hook_corpus.py (#598). template holds {CMD} (or {HEAD} {ARGS}); the safe form puts the inert sentinel there and runs it in bash, the forbidden form puts the payload command there and is only ever judged by the hook. kind: miss (bash ran it, the hook allowed), downgrade (bash ran it, the hook only asked a HIGH shape), false-deny (bash ran nothing, the hook refused). status: fixed (the hook now agrees with bash; replayed as a regression) or boundary (a documented, deliberately conservative refusal; replayed so it stays a refusal). bash/seed/hook record what found it.

A command given several stdin heredocs reads only the last; the hook judges every heredoc body on the line, so a refused command in a discarded earlier body is refused too (conservative by design).

find -exec runs once per match; that the tests match exactly one path is not read, so the hook needs the receipt inside the command.
xargs runs its command once per input batch; a short input makes one batch, but the input is not read, so the hook needs the receipt inside the command.
A loop condition runs once per iteration; that a successful send ends the loop at once is not read, so the hook needs the receipt inside the condition.
